title: 2004 AMC 10A Problem 20
statement: Points \(E\) and \(F\) are located on square \(ABCD\) so that \(\triangle BEF\) is equilateral. What is the ratio of the area of \(\triangle DEF\) to that of \(\triangle ABE?\)

solutions.text:
Let the square have side \(1,\) and by symmetry let \(ED = DF = x,\) so \(AE = 1 - x.\)

Since \(\triangle BEF\) is equilateral, \(EF^2 = EB^2,\) giving \[ 2x^2 = 1 + (1 - x)^2, \] which simplifies to \(x^2 = 2(1 - x).\)

The right triangles have areas \([DEF] = \tfrac12 x^2\) and \([ABE] = \tfrac12(1 - x),\) so \[ \begin{aligned} \dfrac{[DEF]}{[ABE]} &= \dfrac{x^2}{1 - x} \\ &= \dfrac{2(1 - x)}{1 - x} = 2. \end{aligned} \]

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Let the square have side \(1\) and set \(ED = DF = x\)
